title: Urea
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Blood urea and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) are related but are not the same measurement. MedlinePlus describes the BUN test, which measures urea nitrogen, a waste product from protein breakdown, to help check kidney function.
low: For BUN, lower-than-usual levels may be linked to a lack of dietary protein, malnutrition or liver disease.
high: For BUN, higher-than-usual levels may be caused by dehydration, burns, certain medicines, a high-protein diet or a recent heart attack, and in general may mean the kidneys are not working well.
notes: This application has no verified reference interval for urea as distinct from BUN, so it reports a urea value without judging it. Check the interval printed on your own report.
